question: Shan has ₹1218 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Piyush and Manoj and asked them to invest it at 10% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Piyush and Manoj got same amount after 18 and 19 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Shan give to Manoj?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If two amounts invested at R% CI for T₁ and T₂ years respectively yield the same amount, their investment ratio is (1 + R/100)|T¹ − T²|.

Ratio of Piyush's share to Manoj's share = (1 + 10/100)¹⁹ − ¹⁸ = 11/10.

Total parts = 11 + 10 = 21 parts.

Manoj's share = (10 / 21) × 1218 = ₹580.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹580.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount = ₹1218

Rate of interest (R) = 10% compounded annually

Time for Piyush (T₁) = 18 years

Time for Manoj (T₂) = 19 years
